# Dual-runtime Shepherd: Herdr + Durable

## Status

Proposed specification. No behavior change yet.

## Summary

Add a `durable` execution backend to pi-shepherd alongside the existing
`herdr` backend, behind one stable Shepherd surface.

Today pi-shepherd is Herdr-native: `shepherd_spawn` creates a real Herdr
pane with a full `pi` process, tracked in `created-panes.json`, with shared
context in `.shepherd/sessions/` fieldnotes. That stays the default and the
hero.

The new backend runs the same orchestrator pattern — orchestrator launches a
specialist per task, crash-reviewer follows test-driver on failure — as
durable owned conversations + tasks in `@earendil-works/pi-durable`
(`Harness`, `Conversation`, `Submission`, SQLite/Memory storage) instead of
OS processes. Same tool names, same opaque IDs, same agent Markdown
definitions, same agent-facing `shepherd.md` shared memory.

Motivation is a concrete existing workflow plus a concrete new requirement:

1. Existing: orchestrator launches one agent per task to drive the program
   under test; if the app crashes, a different-context agent reviews the
   crash. This must keep working unchanged in Herdr.
2. New: company AI test agent, multi-user, per-user models (free local vs.
   company Copilot subscription), test plans run overnight, report in the
   morning. Herdr panes alone cannot do crash-resume, single-owner
   persistence, usage accounting, or headless operation. Durable can.

## Concept guardrail: no washout

Shepherd's name comes from herding in Herdr, and that concept must not
dilute. To prevent it:

- Shepherd = orchestration pattern (`spawn -> delegate -> watch -> done`,
  visible sheep, shared fieldnotes), not an execution substrate. Herdr is
  today's pasture, durable is the night pen. Same flock.
- Herdr remains default and documented first. `backend: "herdr"` default.
  `/shepherd herd/spawn/read`, 🐑 widget, pane visibility unchanged.
- Durable is opt-in (`backend: "durable" | "auto"`), experimental.
- No durable vocabulary leaks: users see `agent ID / task ID / message ID`,
  never `conversationId / submissionId / pi.live`. `shepherd_read` tails a
  pane *or* a view; caller does not care.
- Files stay agent-facing: `.shepherd/sessions/.../shepherd.md` + per-agent
  notes are the shepherd/sheep shared working memory. They survive
  compaction, waiting, close, timeout, and restart, and are the agents'
  source of truth — never the human handoff. Durable docs mirror them
  transactionally. The morning human report is a separate templated HTML
  file owned by the calling app (e.g. test-report renderer), built from job
  state — it has nothing to do with shepherd internals.
- If the existing test-driver -> crash-reviewer prompt runs unchanged on
  both backends, this spec succeeded. If users must rewrite prompts per
  backend, it failed.

## Goals

- Keep 100% of current Herdr behavior unchanged when `backend: herdr`.
- Run the same orchestrator/specialist workflows headless on durable with
  crash `resume()`, `requestId` dedup, queued steers/follow-ups, and
  usage accounting.
- Reuse agent Markdown definitions (`name/description/tools/model/thinking`)
  on both backends. `model: null/default` inherits Shepherd model on both.
- Map per-user models: Shepherd session per user carries that user's
  default model; children inherit unless pinned (e.g. cheap local triage
  vs. Copilot deep review).
- Bridge fieldnotes to durable docs: single commit writes entry + doc,
  file mirror for inspection.
- Support foreground (return answer) and background (persistent worker,
  survives parent abort) subagents on both backends.
- Keep safety invariants: only close panes shepherd created; raw pane IDs
  never bypass ownership; project agents stay trust-gated with
  `confirmProjectAgents` user-owned.
- Keep `timeout` + `staleWaitThreshold` semantics on both backends
  (durable has no native timeout; shepherd implements via abort).

## Non-goals

- No replacement of Herdr execution. No removal of panes, widgets, or
  `created-panes.json`.
- No requirement to run SQLite to use shepherd. Herdr-only installs keep
  working with no new dependencies.
- No second tool surface. No `durable_spawn` / `herdr_spawn` split in the
  model-facing API. Backend selects inside `shepherd_*`.
- No automatic migration of in-flight Herdr tasks to durable or vice versa.
- No multi-writer SQLite. One process owns durable storage at a time;
  federated multi-host is out of scope (document headless-single-owner
  + optional Herdr tail viewer instead).
- No change to `confirmProjectAgents` security boundary.

## Architecture

### Layout

`src/core/` holds shared domain only. Runtime implementations live under
`src/runtimes/`; the pi-coding-agent surface stays in `src/extension/`:

```text
src/core/            discovery, artifact-sessions, types, ids, config (settings store)
src/runtimes/
  runtime.ts         ShepherdRuntime interface (opaque types only)
  herdr/             current herdr.ts, orchestration.ts, lifecycle.ts (+ messaging.ts support)
  durable/           new runtime.ts + extension.ts
src/extension/       pi-coding-agent tools/commands/settings UI; calls runtime.ts
```

### Runtime interface

Extract what `src/core/{herdr,orchestration,lifecycle}.ts` do today behind
a pure interface; `messaging.ts` moves along as Herdr child I/O support.
Existing Herdr code moves, behavior does not.

```ts
// src/runtimes/runtime.ts (new, no herdr or pi-durable import)
interface ShepherdRuntime {
  spawn(def: AgentDef, opts: { cwd?: string; label?: string; placement?: "pane_right"|"pane_down"|"tab"|"workspace" }): Promise<AgentHandle>
  delegate(agentId: string, task: string, opts: { requestId?: string; timeoutMin?: number }): Promise<TaskId>
  message(target: AgentId | "parent", msg: string, opts: { taskId?: string; expectsReply?: boolean; replyTo?: string; delivery?: "followUp"|"steer" }): Promise<MessageId>
  watch(taskIds: string[]): Promise<Completion[]>
  status(agentId: string): Promise<{ proc: "idle"|"working"|"unknown"; task: "running"|"waiting"|"done"|"blocked"|"failed"; waitingOn?: string; stale?: boolean }>
  close(agentId: string): Promise<void>
  read(agentId: string, opts?: { lines?: number }): Promise<string>
}
```

- `src/core/ids.ts` (new): opaque ID mint/parse — formats and validation
  errors extracted from `LifecycleRegistry` so both runtimes mint and
  validate through one codec.
- `src/runtimes/herdr/` (new): `herdr.ts`, `orchestration.ts`, and
  `lifecycle.ts` move here rename-only and implement the interface;
  `messaging.ts` (child filesystem broker) moves alongside as a support
  module, not an interface implementer.
- `src/runtimes/durable/runtime.ts` (new): implements the same interface
  over pi-durable.
- `src/core/config.ts`: the two-layer settings store moves here from
  `src/extension/config.ts` so runtimes never import the extension layer;
  `/shepherd settings` UI stays in `src/extension/`.
- `src/extension/shepherd.ts`: unchanged tool schemas. Lifecycle calls
  that map 1:1 to the lifecycle-only interface (today: `delegate` and
  `close`) go through it; calls whose results or callbacks the interface
  does not carry (spawn discovery gate, prompt, message result shape,
  watch callbacks, status detail, read source selection) stay on the
  concrete runtime until a later phase needs them. The per-action routing
  record lives in `tasks.md` 0.3.

The interface is lifecycle-only. `/shepherd herd|agents|prune` and the 🐑
widget read runtime introspection (owned-pane/registry summaries,
ownership checks) and keep those accessors on the runtime module in
Phase 0; durable defines its own in Phase 2 (owned conversations/tasks
only). Introspection must not expose native IDs either.

Phase 0 leaves temporary re-export shims at the old `src/core/*` and
`src/extension/config.ts` paths so the existing `verify-*.mjs` suite
passes untouched. Shims and import paths are cleaned up together in
Phase 1.

IDs stay opaque session-scoped strings as today (`shepherd_spawn -> agent
ID`, `shepherd_delegate -> task ID`, `shepherd_message -> message ID`,
reply via `replyTo`). Internally map to `paneId` OR
`{ conversationId, submissionId, taskId }`. Never expose Herdr pane IDs or
durable conversation IDs. Pane IDs remain diagnostic-only for
`shepherd_read`.

### Durable mapping

One sheep = one owned conversation (mirrors pi-durable examples
`22-subagent-foreground`, `23-subagent-background`):

- `spawn` -> `tx.createConversation({ ownership: { kind: "task", taskId: parentTask } })`
  + `configure({ model, thinkingLevel, tools, cwd, instructions })` from
  agent frontmatter. Fresh `pi.provider` identity per sheep (no cache leak
  across users). `placement` ignored; `cwd` honored.
- `delegate` -> `conversation.submit({ type: "input", content: task, requestId })`.
  `requestId` defaults to shepherd task ID. Retried overnight submits dedup
  instead of double-running tests.
- child `shepherd_done` -> completes owner task. Parent `shepherd_watch` ->
  `submission.wait() / harness.waitForTask()`.
- `message` without model impact -> `submit({ type: "write", entry: { kind, data } })`,
  appended immediately even mid-run. With model impact -> steer/follow-up
  (`whenBusy: "steer" | "follow-up"`), queued in `docs["pi.inbox"]`.
- `expectsReply: true` -> durable `waiting` on another task. Reuse
  `staleWaitThreshold` reminder (informational only) + `timeout` as
  authoritative abort -> `blocked`, same as Herdr today.
- `close/abort` -> `conversation.abort()` bottom-up (owned work first),
  queued inputs withdrawn, queued writes stay. `background: true` anchor
  tasks implement today's `stayOpen` persistent workers: survive parent
  abort, reporter task posts answer back as follow-up.
- `status` -> `viewState()` (`entries`, `docs[pi.live, pi.inbox]`) +
  `taskGraph()`. `proc: working` iff live generation/tools running;
  `task: waiting` iff parked on reply.
- `read` -> tail of committed entries + `pi.live` partials/output
  (or `watchEvents()` deltas), not pane scrollback.

Replay policy: test-driving tools that launch apps are NOT `replay: "safe"`.
Crash-interrupted calls yield `interrupted` error results with partial output,
never silent rerun. Only idempotent helpers (read-only git/log readers)
may opt into `replay: "safe"` with keyed `executeTool` reattach.

### Extension duality

pi-shepherd today is `ExtensionAPI from '@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent'`.
pi-durable has its own `defineExtension/defineTool` with
`(args, api, chordContext)` signatures. Keep one shared core, two adapters:

- Shared (no runtime import): `src/core/discovery.ts` (Markdown
  frontmatter: `name/description/tools/model/thinking/omit-*`),
  `src/core/artifact-sessions.ts` (fieldnotes paths/session persistence),
  `src/core/ids.ts` (opaque ID codec), `src/core/types.ts` (tool-schema
  types), and `src/core/config.ts` (settings store + fieldnotes snapshot).
- Adapter-owned: prompt/instructions assembly (depends on the adapter's
  tool list) and runtime introspection.
- `src/extension/*`: the pi-coding-agent surface, unchanged behavior; it
  resolves the active runtime through `src/runtimes/runtime.ts`.
- `src/runtimes/durable/extension.ts` (new): `defineExtension({ name: "shepherd",
  tools: [shepherd, shepherd_spawn, shepherd_delegate, shepherd_message,
  shepherd_prompt, shepherd_watch, shepherd_status, shepherd_close,
  shepherd_read] })` plus the child surface (`shepherd_message` /
  `shepherd_done`) and docs (`ShepherdHerdDoc, ShepherdTasksDoc`). Same
  names and schemas as the pi-coding-agent adapter, including the
  deprecated `shepherd_prompt` compatibility path.

`@earendil-works/pi-durable` + `@earendil-works/chord` become optional
peerDeps. Herdr-only installs must not grow install size or require new
storage.

### Agent definitions

No frontmatter change. Mapping:

| Shepherd md | Durable |
| --- | --- |
| `tools: read, bash` | `configure({ tools })` + `modelTools` narrowing |
| `model: null/default` | inherit Shepherd session model (per-user default) |
| `model: provider/id` | pin (e.g. crash triage on local, deep review on Copilot) |
| `thinking: high` | `thinkingLevel`, clamped per model |
| `omit-system-prompt/docs/context-files` | section resolution at request prep |

Bundled `scout/planner/worker/reviewer` keep working on both. Project
workflow adds e.g. `.agents/agents/test-driver.md` (full tools, captures
logs, never analyzes) and `.agents/agents/crash-reviewer.md` (read-only
bash, never launches app, `thinking: high`, `omit-context-files: true`).
Orchestrator prompt is backend-agnostic:

> Ask test-driver to run plan A. Watch it. On non-zero exit, give its
> fieldnote + log tail to crash-reviewer. Return both.

### Fieldnotes bridge (agent memory, not human report)

Today: `.shepherd/sessions/NNN-orchestrator-<id>/shepherd.md` index +
`<agent>-NN.md` notes. Audience is shepherd + sheep, not humans: shared
working memory so delegated work survives compaction, waiting, close,
timeout, and restart. That agent-truth role is what must be preserved on
durable.

Durable: introduce typed doc mirroring the same content:

```ts
ShepherdNotes = defineDoc<{ index: string; notes: Record<string,string> }>({
  kind: "shepherd.notes", scope: "conversation", history: "rewindable", fork: "asOf", initial: ...
})
```

Write note + entry in one `commit()` (atomic). Mirror to files via `env`
for agent continuity and debugging. Doc is truth for `resume()`; files
are the agents' view. `fieldnotes` setting stays session-scoped (new session after
toggle). Keep `.gitignore` pattern:

```gitignore
.shepherd/*
!.shepherd/config.json
```

### Settings

Extend `ShepherdSettings` with two fields, Herdr defaults preserved:

```jsonc
// ~/.pi/agent/pi-shepherd/config.json
{
  "agentScope": "user", "includeBundledAgents": true,
  "keepOpen": true, "stayOpen": false, "fieldnotes": true,
  "timeout": 20, "staleWaitThreshold": 5,
  "backend": "herdr" // | "durable" | "auto"
}
// .shepherd/config.json adds when active:
// { ..., "durableStorage": "sqlite:./.shepherd/durable.sqlite", "projectScope": true }
```

- `herdr` (default): current behavior, no durable code loaded.
- `durable`: all `shepherd_*` route to durable runtime backed by
  `MemoryStorage` (tests) or `openNodeSqliteStorage(path)` /
  `openNodeJsonlStorage(dir)` (service). WAL `synchronous=NORMAL` noted:
  survives process crash, newest commit may be lost on power failure.
- `auto`: execute on durable, and if Herdr reachable, open read-only tail
  panes fed by `watchEvents()` for visibility. Execution stays durable;
  panes never write.

`/shepherd settings` gains one `backend` row + `durableStorage` row.
`confirmProjectAgents` handling unchanged (user-owned).

`done-nudge` (one reminder turn when child ends turn with open task,
`PI_SHEPHERD_DONE_NUDGES`) maps to durable `onYield` hook on
`GenerationTask`, same one-turn budget, then stall reported as normal
message, never invented status.

## Overnight test-agent profile

Concrete settings for the motivating use case:

- One service process owns `./.shepherd/durable.sqlite`. `harness.resume()`
  on boot. `harness.closed.then(reopen if failed)`.
- One conversation per overnight job, `requestId = jobId`,
  `configure({ model: modelFor(user), cwd: /workspaces/<user>/<job> })`.
  Free-local vs. Copilot resolved at configure time; tokens never land in
  shared docs. Spend via `harness.usage()` per `provider/model` + tool.
- `settings.compaction { reserveTokens, keepRecentTokens, backgroundTokens }`
  tuned for 8h logs; `progress { partialIntervalMs: 100 }` default, raise
  to 500 for remote storage.
- Morning human report is out of shepherd scope: a separate templated HTML
  file owned by the app, rendered by a reporter from the job's report doc
  (e.g. `app.test-report`) + logs via `watchEvents()` snapshot + deltas.
  It must never be `shepherd.md`, a doc snapshot dump, or `/export`.
  Shepherd only guarantees the agent memory it was built from survived.
- Outer job file `jobId -> plan` only as boot re-submitter; `requestId`
  dedup makes it safe.

## Security and safety

- Keep: user discovery default, project agents trust-gated,
  `close` only closes shepherd-created panes (durable: only aborts owned
  conversations/tasks), raw pane IDs rejected, host-user tool permissions
  documented.
- Durable additions: per-user `cwd`/`env` isolation (`env.id` per user or
  container), `modelTools` least-privilege per sheep, `beforeTool` guard
  keeping `crash-reviewer` bash read-only, secrets only in service process
  (never in entries/docs/fieldnotes files committed to git).
- Storage: single-owner SQLite, no NFS multi-writer. Document
  `prefix: "pi_"` namespacing if sharing a DB file with host tables.

## Verification requirements

Implementation is complete only when:

- existing `verify-*.mjs` suite passes on `backend: herdr` (assertions
  unchanged; Phase 1 only rewrites import specifiers);
- new `verify-durable-matrix.mjs` runs `delegate/task-completion/
  task-failures/message-routing/multi-wait/watchers` against
  `MemoryStorage + fauxProvider` on both backends with identical
  orchestrator prompts (test-driver -> crash-reviewer fixture);
- opaque ID contract holds: Herdr pane IDs and durable conversation IDs
  never accepted as `shepherd_*` IDs; `prune/status/read` never leak them;
- crash-resume test: kill mid `bash` on durable, `reopen + resume()`
  yields `interrupted` (unsafe) or reattached result (safe-keyed), no
  double test-run for same `requestId`;
- `expectsReply` waiting + `staleWaitThreshold` reminder + `timeout`
  `blocked` verified on both backends, including cwd-differing agents;
- fieldnotes <-> doc mirror test: note written in same commit as entry,
  file tail matches doc snapshot after restart; `fork: asOf` preserves
  handoff;
- `done-nudge` budget (1 turn, `0` disables) verified via `onYield` on
  durable;
- `npm test` passes; Herdr-only install pulls no durable dependency;
- live checks: `/shepherd herd/spawn/read/settings` on herdr;
  overnight dry-run (submit evening, kill service, resume morning, report
  renders) on durable.

## Migration

No migration. Default `backend: herdr` is current behavior. Opt-in per
workspace via `/shepherd settings` or `.shepherd/config.json`
(`projectScope: true` for teams). Compatibility wrappers from spec 002
(`delegate = start+prompt+wait+close`) remain valid; they compose
primitives regardless of backend.

## Open questions

1. `placement` in durable: ignore vs. map to Herdr tail-viewer panes in
   `auto` mode? Proposal: ignore for execution, honor for viewer.
2. `read --lines` pagination over durable ops frames vs. full view?
   Proposal: tail rendered entries, cap 100 undelivered frames like
   `watch()` does.
3. Compaction of `shepherd.notes` doc on very long overnight runs:
   `rewindable` bounded history vs. summary entry? Needs bench
   (`bench:storage`) before fixing a limit.
4. Should `auto` tail panes be `stayOpen: false` viewers that never accept
   input? Likely yes to avoid dual-write.

## Status — 2026-10-18

- **Scope: implement all of spec 007** (unseen-settlement ledger + settle

  after the review fixes.

## Decisions

- The runtime-neutral seam is a registry observer:
  `onTaskSettled(result, { hadWatchers, agent?, label?, source? })`, fired
  after the watcher fan-out on the transition into a terminal task state.
- The ledger is pure core (`src/core/unseen-completions.ts`, singleton like
  `taskWatcherService`, structural `UnseenSettlement`, no runtime imports);
  delivery policy lives in `src/extension/unseen-completions.ts`.
- The ledger is a queue of **un-noticed** settlements: notify drains the
  entry, so notify-once and loop-safety hold by construction. Entries clear
  on retrieval (watch action) / close (`clearForAgent`, reported) / session
  end.
- Clearing for a late `shepherd_watch` lives in the **watch action**, not
  the watcher notifier: settled tasks are delivered inline inside
  `TaskWatcherService.watch` before the watcher id exists, so the notifier
  never sees them.
- Parent-initiated cancellations (`shepherd_close` → `cancelled`) never
  enter the ledger; neither do `delegateAgent` submission failures (tagged
  `source: "delegate-submission-failure"` — the Shepherd already sees the
  error in the tool result).
- No persistence: the ledger is session-scoped like the task registry.
- The bridge is wired in `index.ts` (parent surface), not in
  `registerShepherdTools`, and subscribes only while a parent session is
  active.

# Journal — 008 sheep on another machine (remote Herdr)

## Status — 2026-10-22

- **Scope: specification only.** No code, no settings, no tool-surface
  change. `specs/008-remote-machine-sheep/` holds `intent.md` and
  `prerequisites.md`; there is no `spec.md`, `plan.md`, or `tasks.md` yet.
- Nothing is implemented: no `machine` spawn attribute, no relay, no
  preflight, no instance manifest, no registry key change.
- Landed on `main` as documentation, not on a feature branch.
- **Exit condition for this stage:** intent (why, who, success, values,
  temptations) and the remote contract (transport direction, version skew,
  install resolution, preflight, rejected alternatives) are written down and
  mutually consistent.

## Decisions

- Transport is **parent → remote push/pull**, not child → parent. Herdr's
  `machine add` already establishes that direction, so the sheep machine
  never needs SSH to the shepherd: no reverse credential, no listener on the
  orchestrator, no tunnel to supervise. A parent-opened `ssh -N -R` tunnel or
  a `restrict`ed key is an opt-in latency optimisation, never a prerequisite.
- Launch assets (script, task, system prompt, session) travel as **content**
  to a **parent-chosen** remote path. Choosing that path is what makes the
  remote mailbox addressable at all.
- The child is launched with the **remote's own** sidecar path
  (`-e <remoteSidecarPath>`) — not the parent's absolute path, and not the
  remote's auto-loaded package. This keeps the child surface identical to
  local: sidecar only, so `shepherd_message` + `shepherd_done`, rather than
  silently granting remote sheep the full `spawn`/`delegate`/`close` surface.
- **Package version is informational; the wire protocol gates.** Envelopes
  already carry `schemaVersion: 1` and reject anything else, and today a
  mismatch dead-letters the envelope so the task hangs to its timeout.
  Mismatch must be refused at `delegate`, with a capability list alongside the
  protocol version.
- **Install method is not part of the identity.** The extension self-reports
  through `$PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/pi-shepherd/instance.json`, so npm, git, a dev
  clone, `-e`, and Nix-store paths resolve the same way. Addressing becomes
  `(machine, agentDir)`; the ownership key becomes
  `(machine, agentDir, paneId)`.
- Provisioning mirrors `herdr machine add`: probe, print the exact install
  line, require interactive approval, round-trip the mailbox, record
  `verifiedAt`. No silent remote install, no silent agent or fieldnotes sync.

## Deliberately not decided

Per-machine default cwd policy, remote model inheritance when the machine
lacks the parent's provider, clock skew against envelope `deadlineAt` /
`completedAt`, fieldnotes for remote sheep, what a repo-controlled remote
`.shepherd/config.json` may influence, and pruning while a machine is powered
off. These stay in `intent.md` until there is code to argue with.

## Next

`spec.md` for the public surface (`machine` spawn attribute, `herd` and
`machine status` output, refusal errors), then `plan.md`/`tasks.md` for phase 1
— inventory, preflight, and the registry key — before any relay work starts.

# Intent — hc-app Runtime (Herdr TUI + hc core)

## Why this exists

pi-shepherd is Herdr-TUI-native today (`herdr` CLI, panes/tabs/workspaces).
The Herdr app (`hc` / herdr-core terminals) is now available in the same
sessions. Users run Shepherd from either place and expect sheep to run
where they are, not cross-spawned into the other UI.

This spec adds a second runtime (`hc`) beside `herdr` behind one Shepherd
surface, with per-command auto-detect and `auto` as default.

This spec is independent from `006-dual-runtime-herdr-durable` (paused).
Same 2-runtimes-1-core pattern, different second runtime.

## Who it serves

1. **TUI user** — runs in `herdr` terminal, sheep appear as panes/tabs.
   Must notice zero change by default.
2. **App user** — runs in `hc` terminal (`HC_TERMINAL_ID`, `hc ls`), sheep
   appear as `hc` terminals. Must get same `spawn -> delegate -> watch ->
   done` flow.
3. **Maintainer** — one tool surface, one agent format, two executors.
   No `herdr_*` vs `hc_*` tool fork.

## What success looks like

- Same orchestrator prompt runs unchanged in TUI and in app.
- Default setting `backend: auto` means: every command runs where it was
  called from, unless the settings UI explicitly pins `herdr` or `hc`.
- Explicit pin is respected but fails cleanly with a hint when that
  runtime is unreachable (no silent cross-spawn).
- The model never chooses a runtime. No `backend` param on any
  `shepherd_*` tool. Backend lives only in settings (app side).
- `shepherd.md` + per-agent fieldnotes stay the shared memory on both.

## Guiding values

1. **Same shepherd, different field.** Tool names, opaque IDs, agent
   Markdown, handoff habits do not fork.
2. **Auto by default.** Detect per command, run local.
3. **No magic / no cross-spawn.** Never spawn a TUI pane from the app
   (or vice versa) unless explicitly pinned *and* reachable.
4. **Boring.** No new deps, no migration, default stays working.

## Why this exists

Spec 007 gave the Shepherd an overnight guarantee: a tracked task that
settles with zero watchers attached is never silent — it surfaces at the
next `agent_before_settle` boundary, or as one coalesced idle wake.
Spec 009 added a second runtime (`hc`) beside Herdr panes behind one
Shepherd surface.

The guarantee currently only holds on one backend. The notice bridge
(`src/extension/unseen-completions.ts`) subscribes to the Herdr
`lifecycleRegistry.onTaskSettled` observer; the `hc` runtime
(`src/runtimes/hc/runtime.ts`) feeds the shared `unseenCompletionLedger`
directly at its own settle point instead of through an equivalent
observer — so an `hc` settle records an entry but never schedules the
coalesced idle wake, never tags `delegate-submission-failure`, and never
passes through the same `hadWatchers` gate the bridge relies on.

parity. `delegate` + no `watch` + chil

  continuation when busy, exactly one `triggerTurn` wake when idle.

Canonical requirement: `worker asks planner while planner is busy → planner
receives the question as a queued follow-up → worker task stays waiting →
planner replies → worker returns to running.` The parent must own request and

   relay a **fresh**-`messageId` copy to a child without the old ack blocking.

# Phase 7 — Task-aware `shepherd_watch` (design notes)

Phase 7 makes `shepherd_watch` observe **tracked tasks** rather than individual
Pi turns. `shepherd_wait` and the legacy prompt watcher remain for
prompt-based flows, but new orchestration uses tasks.

## Core idea

Tasks settle only from explicit lifecycle events (a child calling
`shepherd_done`, or an explicit failure / cancellation / timeout). Because that
settlement always flows through `LifecycleRegistry.settleTask()`, the registry
already has a single, authoritative settlement point. The task watcher hooks

# Phase 8 — Stale-wait monitoring (design notes)

Phase 8 adds a *non-invasive* nudge for a tracked task that is sitting in the
`waiting` state — i.e. waiting on a required reply that has not yet arrived —
for longer than a configurable threshold. It never settles a task; it only
informs the parent that something has been waiting a long time.

## What counts as "stale"

A task is stale when **all** of these hold:

1. `task.state === 'waiting'` — the task has entered the `waiting` state.
2. `task.pendingReplyMessageId` is set — there is a specifically expected reply
   (an `expectsReply` question, or a child mirror of one). A task that is
   `waiting` for any other reason (a bare `agent_end`, a manual `setTaskWaiting`
   with no outstanding reply) is *not* stale by definition, because there is no
   reply to time out.
3. `now - task.waitingSince >= staleWaitThreshold` (minutes, from settings).
4. `task.staleNotifiedAt` is unset — the monitor has not yet nudged for this
   waiting episode.

# Asynchronous Shepherd Tasks and Agent Messaging

## Status

Implemented specification.

## Summary

Add asynchronous task coordination and conversational messaging to
pi-shepherd. A delegated task and an agent conversation are separate concerns:

a delegated task is tracked until it explicitly completes, while messages can
be sent between the Shepherd and agents, or between agents, without blocking
the sender or consuming the recipient's task slot.

The design must not infer task completion from a Pi turn ending, an `agent_end`
event, an `agent_settled` event, or the child process becoming idle. An agent
may finish a turn because it is waiting for another agent's response and may
resume the same delegated task later.

The intended workflow is:

```text
shepherd_delegate
  -> tracked task starts
  -> child sends shepherd_message to another participant
  -> child task enters waiting state
  -> child's current Pi turn settles
  -> recipient eventually replies with shepherd_message
  -> child receives a queued 
…[内容超出评审预算——仅保留首尾各 1024 字符]…

- message routing rejects unknown targets and invalid sender capabilities;
- messages do not create fieldnotes unless explicitly associated with a task;
- status and the TUI widget show an idle process with a waiting task; and
- parent shutdown cleans up broker resources without losing already-persisted
  task outcomes.

Live Herdr verification must cover at least:

1. Shepherd delegates a task to scout.
2. Scout sends a question to a busy planner.
3. Scout's turn settles and its task remains waiting.
4. Planner eventually receives and answers the queued question.
5. Scout resumes and calls `shepherd_done`.
6. `shepherd_watch` receives the final task result.
7. A stale-wait notification is delivered when the planner does not answer
   within the configured threshold.
8. Closing or timing out either participant produces the correct terminal
   task state.

# Smoke forensics

## hc: before/after snapshot

```sh
for d in /tmp/pi-shepherd-broker-*/; do
  s=$(python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('$d/broker.json'))['sessionId'])" 2>/dev/null)
  echo "$s $d"
done | sort > /tmp/smoke-before.txt
# ... run the smoke ...
# ... same loop to /tmp/smoke-after.txt, then:
comm -13 /tmp/smoke-before.txt /tmp/smoke-after.txt   # new dirs: expect only the session broker
```

Reload nuance: each process lifetime mints one broker dir per
session, so a reload between snapshots legitimately shows one new
session dir (same sessionId, new brokerId; the old dir is inert —
no process or timer references it). Take both snapshots within one
process lifetime, and expect exactly one live store.

## hc: junk check

Any new dir whose `broker.json` sessionId starts with `hc-parent-`
is a fallback-keyed junk store minted by a bare `ensureBroker()` on a
path that should have threaded the drain's session-keyed broker.
Zero is the only passing number.

## Timing interpretation

- Settle lag after the done lands in `parent/inbox` (or moves to
  `parent/processed/`): **< 10 s** means a live drain path consumed it
  (background tick or tool-call drain). Near the delegate deadline
  means only the deadline drain fired — the prompt paths are broken.
- Caveat: the 250 ms tick consumes inbox files fast, so inbox
  *presence* polls can miss arrivals entirely. Detect arrival via new
  files in `parent/processed/` (they persist), not via inbox
  non-emptiness.
- Status-view caveat: the view carries unsettled tasks only. Task gone
  + agent known = settled.

## herdr

No `/tmp` session brokers. Forensics are pane-scoped inbox dirs (see
`src/runtimes/herdr/messaging.ts` `inboxPath`) plus the owned-pane
registry (`created-panes.json`). Raw pane ids must never bypass the
ownership check on close.
